synthesis: Fourier support acts as an arithmetic-resolution threshold whose newly visible off-diagonal channel depends on the family and on sign conditioning: the mixed family retains the common orthogonal density, fixed-sign families acquire opposite Kloosterman corrections, and symmetric squares acquire a Poisson zero-mode correction producing the symplectic kernel.
source_support: Unit u03 states that support below one is diagonal and that crossing one introduces Kloosterman contributions. Unit u07 shows that the parity-mixed weight-aspect average still has only the common O main term through support two. Units u11 and u15 separately derive the |xi|>=1 fixed-sign correction from principal-character Kloosterman terms, with the parity/root-number sign selecting SO(even) versus SO(odd). Unit u13 instead factors the prime-square Kloosterman sum and isolates a Poisson zero mode that supplies the symplectic correction.
nonparaphrase_operation: Compares the fate of the same beyond-diagonal Fourier region across three averaging structures and identifies the selector in each: parity mixing cancels the sign-sensitive term, root-number conditioning preserves it with opposite signs, and square-factorization plus Poisson summation selects a coherent zero mode for the symmetric-square family.
limits: The fixed-sign orthogonal conclusions assume relevant GRH and support inside (-2,2); the symmetric-square conclusion assumes GRH and support inside (-4/3,4/3). The source proves restricted-support density limits, not unrestricted density conjectures, and its dense intermediate constants and formulas remain scan-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because the relation needs distinct units: u07 supplies the mixed-family baseline, u11/u15 supply parity-specific off-diagonal survival, and u13 supplies a different off-diagonal extraction mechanism. Together they support a concrete support-to-arithmetic-channel comparison unavailable from any one parent, while u03 explicitly frames the threshold.

synthesis: A GL1-type prime-progression cancellation estimate enters the GL2 density calculation at the new Bessel off-diagonal, extends the usable Fourier bandwidth, and only then can a positive band-limited test turn the family-average bound into an exclusion for each real off-line zero.
source_support: Unit u05 states Hypothesis 4, the support extension from (-2,2) to (-7/3,7/3), and Corollary 6. Unit u08 locates the exact analytic interface: beyond the former Bessel-decay range, residue-class decomposition produces F_{a,c}, and Hypothesis 4 plus integration by parts makes that term o(K) through support 7/3. Unit u09 chooses a nonnegative sinc-square test with that bandwidth; positivity bounds each zero term, while evaluation at an imaginary ordinate gives hyperbolic growth and beta<=13/14.
nonparaphrase_operation: Composes three distinct interfaces into a conditional implication chain: prime cancellation controls the Bessel-Kloosterman remainder, that control enlarges Fourier visibility, and positivity converts the enlarged average density into an individual zero-location bound. This identifies why cancellation alone does not yield the corollary and why the bandwidth numerically determines its boundary.
limits: The support extension requires Hypothesis 4; the stated individual conclusion also assumes every zero is either on the critical line or real and applies only for sufficiently large weight. It excludes real zeros above 13/14 rather than proving RH or treating general complex off-line zeros; weaker prime-sum exponents below 3/4 yield only an unspecified support improvement.
quality_reason: Accepted because u08 provides the mechanism missing from the theorem statement in u05, while u09 supplies a separate positivity and growth argument needed to pass from an averaged density theorem to an individual real-zero exclusion. The synthesis preserves both independent hypotheses and does not promote the conditional quasi-RH bridge to an unconditional result.

synthesis: Beyond-diagonal density information becomes an improved nonvanishing bound only after the admissible test is reoptimized: a nonconstant Fourier correction makes sinc-square suboptimal, Paley-Wiener factorization converts positivity into a quadratic operator problem, and the resulting Fredholm equation yields symmetry-specific extremizers and strict gains.
source_support: Unit u16 defines the band-limited extremum, proves that nonconstant m_G makes the usual sinc-square test nonoptimal, and translates a smaller extremal value into strict parity-specific nonvanishing or vanishing-order bounds. Unit u17 factors every admissible nonnegative test as |h|^2, rewrites the objective as <(I+K)g,g>/|<g,1>|^2, treats the singular case, and derives (I+K)f_0=1 in the applicable nonsingular case. Unit u18 solves the SO(even) and SO(odd) equations explicitly and substitutes their values into sharper proportions.
nonparaphrase_operation: Carries information through two representation changes that no parent supplies alone: from a density kernel to a constrained positive-test extremum, then from nonnegative band-limited functions to inversion of a convolution operator, and finally from the kernel's symmetry to explicit orthogonal extremizers and arithmetic proportions.
limits: The gains inherit the density theorems' GRH and support restrictions and are conditional on the corresponding symmetry kernels. The mixed O correction is constant, so this route gives no strict mixed-family gain without separating parity; the symmetric-square case establishes strict improvement but these parents do not compute an analogous explicit extremal value. Extraction-sensitive trigonometric constants should not be reused literally without scan verification.
quality_reason: Accepted because u16 establishes both the optimization need and its arithmetic consequence, u17 supplies the essential Paley-Wiener/Fredholm representation change, and u18 demonstrates that solving the operator problem yields the claimed sharper orthogonal bounds. This is a concrete dependency across three units, not a thematic combination.
